turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm sitting down. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have about twenty minutes. Owen's zero is still in the gradebook, and nobody called me before it went in.
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.
"The end of it." That's a machine's guess, and the company that sells it says not to use it alone. Your own procedure, 4.3, says the same, so what else do you have?
I don't need more proof than that.
"Don't need more proof." I'm writing that down. Withdraw the zero and apologize to Owen, or I'm walking into the principal's office when we're done here.
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.
"Unlike some people." Say who you mean. My child never lies, so are you calling me a liar too?
"Zero stands." Entered before anyone spoke to Owen, before anyone called me, and on a score you can't show me how you checked. I'm writing down the time, and the principal is next.
